title: Betrayed by a Friend
speaker: Ryan Baird
summary: Jesus endured abandonment by his closest friends. In Judas and Peter we see two paths, and in Peter the hope of the gospel.
exhortation: When Jesus was betrayed, it wasn't just by an acquaintance, the mob or the Pharisees. It was by those who walked with him, embraced him, wept with him and prayed with him, those who went out on mission at his command and did his works.

Judas begins betraying Jesus in the deepest way one person can betray another. Jesus feels the crushing pain of a close friend he worked and planned with now scheming to do him evil, for thirty pieces of silver. It begins an abandonment that continues all the way to the cross, his closest friends leaving him one after another. John 13:21 says Jesus "was troubled in his spirit, and testified, 'Truly, truly, I say to you, one of you will betray me.'" He felt the agony of his friends turning on him.

And it gets worse. Peter, who said he would face death with him, cowers at the question of a servant girl. The betrayer finds Jesus in the hour of darkness as he sweats drops of blood in Gethsemane. Matthew 26:48 says, "Now the betrayer had given them a sign, saying, 'The one I will kiss is the man; seize him.'" Judas takes the kindness and affection meant to come from a friend and makes it his crowning act of evil, fulfilling Psalm 41:9: "Even my close friend in whom I trusted... has lifted his heel against me." Jesus endured a level of abandonment we can only begin to fathom, and to all of it was added the greatest separation imaginable: the Son of God cut off from the love of the Father.

In these two men, Judas and Peter, we see the two paths offered to each of us. Judas chose money and gave himself wholly over to evil. But in Peter we see the hope of the gospel. Even someone who broke a vow made directly to the face of Christ can turn and repent. And far from scowling or scolding, our Savior pursues Peter and gives him the chance to look on the one he betrayed and love him once more. What a Savior.
prayer: Lord, our hearts are filled with gratitude as we see the mercy and grace you pour out on us: that you would save sinners and die for enemies, for those who shrink back in the battle. You restore, you strengthen and you pursue.

I pray for anyone listening that whatever sin is weighing them down would not keep them from you any longer, but that they would repent. You are quick to forgive, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love, and you will not despise a broken and contrite heart. In fact, you draw near to it. As we contemplate the cross this week and look at your sacrifice, help us see your love for the sinner and your pursuit of the repentant. In Jesus' name.
